subject: Accounting
title: The 16th Amendment
description: A quick win: understand The 16th Amendment.

hook.text: In 1913, the U.S. Constitution was amended to permanently allow federal income tax.

buildup.text: Before the 16th Amendment, the federal government relied on tariffs and excise taxes for revenue.

discovery.text: The Supreme Court had ruled a prior income tax unconstitutional. The amendment fixed that.

twist.text: The original top rate was just 7%. By World War II, it reached 94%.

climax.text: The amendment gave Congress unlimited power to tax income—a power debated fiercely ever since.

punchline.text: Seven percent became ninety-four. Rates never stand still.

details.summary: The 16th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, ratified in 1913, gave Congress the power to levy a federal income tax, permanently changing American fiscal policy and creating the revenue system that funds the federal government today.
details.whyItMatters: The 16th Amendment made the federal income tax constitutional, creating the primary funding mechanism for the U.S. federal government and reshaping the relationship between citizens and their government.
takeaways: The 16th Amendment was ratified in 1913, making a federal income tax permanently constitutional
Before the amendment, the federal government relied primarily on tariffs and excise taxes for revenue
The income tax now provides roughly half of all federal government revenue

faq.question: What did the 16th Amendment do?
faq.answer: It authorized Congress to levy an income tax on individuals and businesses without apportioning it among the states based on population, as the original Constitution required. This made a national income tax practical and constitutional for the first time.

faq.question: How did the U.S. fund itself before the income tax?
faq.answer: Before 1913, the federal government relied primarily on tariffs (taxes on imported goods) and excise taxes (taxes on specific products like alcohol and tobacco). These revenue sources limited what the federal government could spend on, keeping it much smaller than it is today.
